idiom_name: value types with copy-on-write (Array/Dictionary/Set/String) + isKnownUniquelyReferenced for custom storage
implementation_notes: Swift carries the pattern in the language's value semantics: the Swift array design document states that the Array types 'have full value semantics via copy-on-write (COW)' - variables share the backing buffer until one of them mutates, at which point the storage is copied - and Dictionary, Set and String behave the same way, so the classic counted handle is absorbed rather than written. A custom value type that silos its state in a class adds the check itself with isKnownUniquelyReferenced(_:), documented as 'useful for implementing the copy-on-write optimization for the deep storage of value types', copying the storage when the answer is false. What Swift does not provide is the thread-safe half: the uniqueness check and ARC's retain counts are non-atomic operations on shared storage, so a snapshot shared between threads must be published atomically and treated as immutable (immutable lets, an actor, or a lock around mutation), not merely copy-on-write.
pitfalls: Copy-on-write is not thread-safety: two threads mutating 'the same' value race on the uniqueness check, and Apple's documentation warns that if the instance 'is being accessed by multiple threads simultaneously, this function may still return true' - which it calls undefined behaviour, so share immutable snapshots or serialise mutation.

Sharing is invisible: let b = a then mutating a copies only when the storage is shared, so a large value copied once per mutation can still dominate a hot loop, and a class-backed custom type that forgets the uniqueness check silently mutates its 'copies'.

The uniqueness check is fragile in expressions: Apple's own example shows that myStorage.shouldCopy || !isKnownUniquelyReferenced(&myStorage) re-copies on every call in debug builds because the left-hand side still holds a reference - store the condition in a local or put the check first.
sources: Swift repository documentation, docs/Arrays.md - 'The ArrayTypes have full value semantics via copy-on-write (COW)' with the sharing-until-mutation example: https://github.com/swiftlang/swift/blob/main/docs/Arrays.md

Apple Developer Documentation, isKnownUniquelyReferenced(_:) - the copy-on-write hook for deep storage of value types, its weak/unowned caveat, and the multi-thread warning: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/swift/isknownuniquelyreferenced(_:)-5kvtu
